container: Genetic engineering offers powerful ways to prevent disease, improve crops, and create medicines. It may help families avoid inherited conditions and allow farmers to grow food with fewer chemicals. Yet changing genes raises serious questions about safety, fairness, and control. Unexpected effects could harm ecosystems or future generations. Expensive treatments may widen inequality if only wealthy people can access them. Society must decide which changes are acceptable and who should make those choices. Clear rules, independent research, and public discussion can reduce risks. Genetic engineering should be guided by caution, transparency, and respect for life.
